subject: Whether extracting billing from the Rails monolith into a separate service is the right and feasible way to meet audit finding AF-2026-09's 'logical segregation' requirement by 30 April 2027, including effort and schedule risk
decisionObjective: The exec meeting needs to decide how to close audit finding AF-2026-09 by 30 April 2027. That means choosing between full service extraction and cheaper controls the auditor also accepts (database-level access controls, separate schemas with restricted roles, segregation of duties, audit logging), and judging how likely each option is to finish in time. The request asks for an exact engineer-month figure and a firm yes/no. The plan has no phase estimates and the coupling analysis is incomplete, so the evaluation should produce a defensible range with explicit uncertainty and the conditions that would turn it into a yes or a no. It should not invent false precision.

criteria.name: Fit to the audit requirement
criteria.rationale: AF-2026-09 asks for restricted access to billing data and code paths, segregation of duties and change audit logging, and it explicitly does not prescribe an architecture. The option chosen has to produce controls the auditors can see working. A finished extraction that lacks access controls and audit logging would still fail, and lighter options may be enough.

criteria.name: Schedule feasibility against 30 April 2027
criteria.rationale: The exec wants a yes/no on meeting the deadline. Planned staffing is 4 engineers at 50% from January, which is about 2 FTE over roughly 4 months, or about 8 engineer-months of capacity before the deadline. That capacity has to be compared with realistic effort, including dual-write and cutover phases that cannot be compressed.

criteria.name: Effort estimate credibility, calibrated to history
criteria.rationale: The three past extractions overran their estimates by about 1.8x, 2.6x and 2.4x. Any engineer-month figure has to be adjusted for this record and stated as a range, not one exact number.

criteria.name: Scope and coupling uncertainty
criteria.rationale: 214 files reference Billing::, shared tables have not been analysed, and the background-job scan is incomplete (at least 17 jobs). These unknowns drive both the effort and the risk of a failed cutover, and they are what currently make an exact estimate impossible.

criteria.name: Delivery readiness and execution risk
criteria.rationale: The plan has no owner, every phase is marked TBD, and staffing is part-time. Weak governance makes slippage more likely and affects whether a firm commitment is credible at all.

criteria.name: Fallback and interim compliance path
criteria.rationale: If extraction overruns, the company needs interim controls such as DB roles, schema separation or audit logging that can satisfy the auditors by the deadline while extraction continues, so that missing the deadline does not mean failing the audit.

assumptionsToVerify.assumption: Extracting billing into its own service is needed, or is the right way, to satisfy the auditors' 'logical segregation' requirement.
assumptionsToVerify.howToCheck: Compare against the text of AF-2026-09, which says no architecture is prescribed and DB-level controls or separate schemas are acceptable. Confirm with the auditors what evidence they expect.

assumptionsToVerify.assumption: An exact engineer-month figure can be produced for the extraction.
assumptionsToVerify.howToCheck: Check whether bottom-up phase estimates and a complete coupling analysis exist. Currently all phases are TBD and the dependency analysis is partial, so only a range calibrated to history can be justified.

assumptionsToVerify.assumption: A firm yes/no on completion before 30 April 2027 can be given.
assumptionsToVerify.howToCheck: Compare calibrated effort ranges with confirmed capacity. Report a probability or conditional answer unless the range sits entirely above or below the available capacity.

assumptionsToVerify.assumption: The audit deadline is 30 April 2027 and the requirement is 'logical segregation'.
assumptionsToVerify.howToCheck: Confirm the deadline date and wording against the formal audit finding or the auditor correspondence. The attached finding does not state a date.

assumptionsToVerify.assumption: Staffing of 4 engineers at 50% from January gives about 8 engineer-months before the deadline.
assumptionsToVerify.howToCheck: Recompute from confirmed start date, allocation, holidays and on-call load. Confirm with engineering leadership that these engineers are committed.

assumptionsToVerify.assumption: The historical overrun ratios (18/10=1.8, 13/5=2.6, 16.8/7=2.4) apply to the billing extraction.
assumptionsToVerify.howToCheck: Recompute the ratios from estimate-history.csv and check that the past projects are comparable in scope, team and coupling.

evidenceByGap.question: What exactly will the auditors accept as evidence of 'logical segregation' by 30 April 2027? Would database-level access controls or separate schemas with restricted roles, plus segregation of duties and change audit logging, fully close AF-2026-09 without extracting a service?

evidence.claim: Audit finding AF-2026-09 requires that access to billing data and billing code paths be restricted to authorised roles, with segregation of duties and audit logging of changes. It states that the auditors do not prescribe an architecture, and that database-level access controls, separate schemas with restricted roles, or service extraction are all acceptable if the controls are demonstrable.
evidence.applicability: G1 and the assumption that extraction is required. The finding's own text says extraction is not necessary, so lighter controls can close the finding if they are demonstrable.
evidence.limitations: This is a two-sentence summary, not the full finding. It does not define what 'demonstrable' evidence is, it names no testing period, and it does not say whether the auditor wants the controls operating effectively over a period or only designed and implemented.

evidence.claim: The user states that the auditors require billing to be 'logically segregated' from the Rails monolith by 30 April 2027, and that engineering leadership wants to extract billing into its own service to satisfy this.
evidence.applicability: The deadline and the framing of the requirement. Neither the phrase 'logically segregated' nor the date 30 April 2027 appears in the supplied audit-finding.md, which also says extraction is not required.
evidence.limitations: The deadline and wording could not be checked against the formal finding or auditor correspondence. The supplied finding contains no date.

evidence.claim: pgAudit is a PostgreSQL extension that provides session audit logging (statements by class, e.g. READ, WRITE, DDL) and object audit logging (statements affecting particular relations, controlled through pgaudit.role, limited to SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE). Its stated goal is 'to produce audit logs often required to comply with government, financial, or ISO certifications.' The README states 'pgAudit supports PostgreSQL 14 or greater' and 'Audit logging is best-effort and not transactional.'
evidence.applicability: G1 and C6. Database-level change audit logging on billing tables is available off the shelf and does not require extracting a service, which supports a lighter or interim compliance path.
evidence.limitations: This only applies if the monolith uses PostgreSQL, and the supplied documents do not name the database engine. 'Best-effort and not transactional' could matter for audit evidence. A search snippet said PostgreSQL 13+, while the fetched README says 14+, so the version floor depends on the README version. Database audit logs do not cover code-path access or segregation of duties in deployment on their own.

evidence.claim: PostgreSQL GRANT gives no public access by default for tables, columns and schemas. The schema USAGE privilege lets a role look up objects in a schema, and each object's own privileges still apply. Roles can be granted to other roles. Superusers bypass object privileges.
evidence.applicability: G1 and C6. Separate schemas with restricted roles are a standard database mechanism and match the option the finding explicitly accepts.
evidence.limitations: Search snippet only. The WebFetch of www.postgresql.org failed (host not allowed in this session's network settings). The two refs are an official page and a vendor mirror of the same documentation, so they are not truly independent, and this is kept at INFERRED. The superuser bypass means segregation of duties also has to cover who holds superuser or DBA access. Applicable only if the database is PostgreSQL.

evidence.claim: Practitioner and exam-prep sources describe ITGC audit evidence for logical access (access listings, tickets, approvals, review sign-offs), segregation of duties (role matrices showing requester, approver and administrator are different people; developers without production deploy rights) and change management (sampled change tickets with authorisation, testing and deployment segregation). They note that SoD gaps and missing change approvals are frequent causes of findings.
evidence.applicability: G1 and G6. Auditors typically test whether controls are operating, through access reviews, approvals and logs, rather than the system's architecture. A 'finished' extraction without these controls would not by itself produce the evidence auditors sample.
evidence.limitations: Based only on search-result summaries; no page was fetched. Most sources are not primary standards (PCAOB AS 2201, COBIT and NIST 800-53 were not inspected). This is general practice and cannot stand in for confirmation from this company's auditor.

evidenceByGap.question: Which database tables does billing share with other domains, and how many write paths outside billing touch billing data?

evidence.claim: The static analysis of billing coupling (partial, 2026-10) found 214 files referencing the Billing:: namespace. Shared DB tables between billing and other domains are 'not yet analysed'. Background jobs touching invoices number 'at least 17 (scan incomplete)'.
evidence.applicability: G2, G3 and C4. The main scope drivers are unquantified, so an exact estimate cannot be justified.
evidence.limitations: The analysis is partial. Shared tables and write paths outside billing are unknown, and the job count is a lower bound. A file reference count does not measure coupling depth.

evidence.claim: Practitioner guidance on strangler-fig extractions says application-level dual writes risk data discrepancies, and that outbox or change-data-capture patterns are safer. Shared-database sync bridges should be time-boxed or they tend to become permanent. Migrating data ownership is called the most dangerous step and is best done last.
evidence.applicability: G2 and C2/C4. Phases 2 (dual-write ledger) and 3 (invoice cutover) carry the most risk and are hard to compress. Their effort depends on the unanalysed shared tables (E4).
evidence.limitations: Practitioner blogs, opinion rather than standards. Search snippets only, not fetched. There is no quantitative effort data.

evidence.claim: The billing extraction plan (draft) has four phases: Phase 1 identify boundaries (TBD), Phase 2 dual-write ledger (estimate TBD), Phase 3 cut over invoices (TBD), Phase 4 decommission monolith billing code (TBD). Owner: unassigned. Staffing: 4 engineers at 50% from January.
evidence.applicability: G4, G5 and C5. No phase has an estimate, so a bottom-up engineer-month figure cannot be built from the plan. Ownership is missing. Nominal capacity is 4 x 0.5 = 2 FTE.

evidence.claim: Estimate history (estimated vs actual engineer-months): search-service extraction 10 vs 18, notifications extraction 5 vs 13, auth extraction 7 vs 16.8.
evidence.applicability: G4, G7 and C3. The planner's ratios (1.8x, 2.6x, 2.4x, mean about 2.27x) are consistent with these raw figures. Every past extraction overran by at least 1.8x.
evidence.limitations: Only three data points. There is no information on the size, coupling, team or causes of the overruns, so whether billing is comparable (G7) cannot be judged. Billing involves financial data and a dual-write ledger, which may make it riskier than the reference class, but there is no evidence either way. Ratios have not been recomputed at this stage.

evidence.claim: Reference class forecasting (Flyvbjerg) corrects the planning fallacy by placing a project within the outcome distribution of similar past projects (the 'outside view'). A PMI paper notes the approach is 'highly institution and domain specific', and one of its datasets showed little or no planning fallacy.
evidence.applicability: G4, G7 and C3. This supports using the company's own extraction history (E5) as an institution-specific reference class and stating effort as a range, not a point estimate.
evidence.limitations: Neither page was fetched; the support comes from search summaries across two domains. A reference class of three projects is very small. Industry overrun figures that appeared in the results (e.g. TechCrunch's 107% cost overrun) come from unnamed surveys and were not recorded as evidence.

unresolvedGaps.reason: The supplied finding says lighter controls are acceptable 'if controls are demonstrable', but what evidence and testing period the auditor expects can only be confirmed with the auditor directly. The formal deadline and the 'logical segregation' wording are not in the supplied finding.
Shared DB tables and write paths outside billing are 'not yet analysed' (dependency-analysis.md). This is internal data that cannot be researched externally.
The background-job scan is incomplete ('at least 17'). A full inventory needs internal code analysis.
All phases are TBD, so no bottom-up base exists to apply the 1.8x-2.6x overrun ratios to.
The start date (January of an unstated year), the engineers' commitment, holidays and on-call load are not confirmed. The plan has no owner.

The finding does not define 'done'. Whether Phase 4 decommissioning is needed for compliance has to be confirmed with the auditor. General ITGC practice (E8, snippets only) suggests auditors test the controls in operation rather than the architecture.
estimate-history.csv gives no size, coupling, team or overrun-cause data for search, notifications or auth, so comparability with billing cannot be assessed.

WebFetch of www.postgresql.org failed (ENOTFOUND, the host is not in the session's allowed network domains). Access-control documentation is backed only by search snippets. The database engine of the monolith is not stated in the supplied documents.
